# Intake Brief: Review Queue depth notification is incorrect (AH-0MUDYTQ55002NUSJ)

## Headline

When the herdr worklist review queue is deep, the footer banner currently always
says "— audits will drain it". It must instead say "— focus on audits" while any
review item still lacks a current audit, and "Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')" once
every review item is audited.

## Problem statement

The herdr worklist shows a review-queue-depth banner when the root-only
`completed/in_review` count reaches `browseItemCount`. Today the banner copy is
fixed ("… — audits will drain it"), so it gives the same instruction whether
audits are still outstanding or the queue is fully audited and ready to ship.
The copy should reflect the actual audit state so the producer knows whether to
keep running audits or to ship.

## Users

- **Producer / sprint lead** — reads the banner to decide the next action.
  - *User story:* As a producer, when the review queue is deep and some items
    still need auditing, I want the banner to say "focus on audits" so I know
    audits are the drain. When every item in the queue has a current audit, I
    want the banner to say "Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')" so I know I can ship.
- **Downtime dispatcher / operator** — must be unaffected: the banner is
  display-only and never gates dispatch (WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the review queue is deep (root-only `completed/in_review` count ≥
   `browseItemCount`) **and** at least one root-level `in_review` item has an
   outstanding audit, the footer banner text reads exactly:
   `Review queue deep (<completed> of <browseItemCount> completed/in_review) — focus on audits`.
2. When the review queue is deep **and** no root-level `in_review` item has an
   outstanding audit, the footer banner text reads exactly:
   `Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')`.
3. "Outstanding audit" is determined by the existing audit-freshness semantics
   (`isAuditFresh` / `inReviewBucket`): an `in_review` item with no stored
   `auditedAt`, or whose stored audit is not current, counts as outstanding. A
   fresh, passed audit does not.
4. The banner remains display-only: it never disables downtime dispatch, never
   writes/clears `.herdr-downtime-disabled`, and does not change code-freeze
   banner behaviour or the `showHelpText` gate.
5. Automated tests assert the exact rendered banner text for both variants and
   for the boundaries (deep+outstanding → deep+none; deep → shallow), using the
   existing worklist render test seams.
6. All related documentation/code comments describing the banner are updated to
   the new copy and the outstanding-audit condition.

## Constraints

- **Source repository:** the banner is implemented in the **ContextHub** repo
  (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`), not in `AI_Hell`. This work item is tracked
  in the `AI_Hell` worklog (consistent with existing tooling work items such as
  AH-0MUDYHPPC008F7PV); implementation must target the ContextHub source tree.
- `browseItemCount` default 20, re-read live from settings (no restart).
- Root-only counting via `wl list --status completed --stage in_review
  --root-only --json` (same query as `fetchCompletedItemCount`).
- No new persistence mechanism; reuse existing fetch helpers where possible.
- Display-only; must not reintroduce the sprint-complete auto-disable
  (WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD RCA root cause A).
- Keep the change minimal: banner copy + the state needed to choose it.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` renders the banner in the footer branch
  (~3596–3617): `const bannerText = \`Review queue deep${countDisplay} — audits will drain it\`;`
  where `countDisplay` = ` (<completed> of <browseItemCount> completed/in_review)`.
- `refreshSprintState()` (~4531–4546) calls `fetchCompletedItemCount()`
  (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` ~684) and sets
  `sprintComplete = count >= liveBrowseCount`. Only a count is retained —
  per-item audit state is not currently available to the banner.
- `fetchCompletedItemCount()` runs `wl list --status completed --stage in_review
  --root-only --json` and returns the item count. `wl list --json` items expose
  `stage`, `status`, `auditedAt`, `auditResult`, `fingerprint`, `updatedAt`
  (but not `currentFingerprint`).
- Audit freshness is centralised: `isAuditFresh(...)` in
  `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` (~306) and the audit-aware bucket predicate
  `inReviewBucket(...)` in `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` (~360–389). The
  audit-dispatch tier uses the same predicate.
- There are currently **no automated tests** covering the banner text or
  `refreshSprintState` — this gap must be closed.

## Desired change

- Extend the banner-state refresh (or add a sibling helper) so it knows whether
  any root-level `in_review` item has an outstanding audit, in addition to the
  deep-queue boolean.
- Select the banner copy from that state:
  - outstanding audits → `Review queue deep (<n> of <browseItemCount> completed/in_review) — focus on audits`;
  - none outstanding → `Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')`.
- Add regression tests for both variants and the transition boundaries.
- Update the code comments that describe the banner to match the new copy and
  condition.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — banner copy selection in the footer render
  branch (~3596–3617); `refreshSprintState` (~4531–4546); render-option plumbing
  for `sprintComplete` / `sprintCompletedCount` (~3359–3396, ~5893–5894).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchCompletedItemCount` (~681–699): extend
  or replace with an outstanding-audit-aware fetch of root `completed/in_review`
  items.
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh` (~306) shared freshness
  predicate to reuse.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — `inReviewBucket` (~360–389) audit-aware
  predicate (alternative reuse).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — regression tests for both banner
  variants and boundaries.

## Related work

- **WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD** (ContextHub, done/deleted) — P2: replaced the
  sprint-complete auto-disable with the review policy; introduced the current
  "audits will drain it" banner copy.
- **WL-0MTHSHN5V008R5L0** (ContextHub, completed) — Auto-disable dispatching when
  sprint is complete; original sprint-complete banner ("Sprint Complete, hit S to
  ship").
- **WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG** (ContextHub, completed) — Allow `/skill:audit` on
  complete/in_review items without a valid audit; defines the "valid audit"
  (`isAuditFresh`) semantics reused here.
- **WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY** (ContextHub, completed) — Ship It shortcut ('S') with
  typed confirmation dispatching `/skill:ship release`.
- **WL-0MUDEJU9Z004UO2W** (ContextHub, blocked/plan_complete) — worklist
  pre-dialog ship gate + freeze-on-confirm integration (Ship Guard interaction).
- **WL-0MT2UQWOR007CYY9** (ContextHub, completed) — review-queue-depth gate for
  non-critical implement dispatch.
- **WL-0MU8808ZY0091JIA** (ContextHub, completed) — surface held gate in header
  (recent banner/header area change).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "outstanding audit" scope.** Defined as a **root-level**
  `in_review` item with no `auditedAt` or a non-current audit, matching the
  banner's root-only count. If child `in_review` items should also suppress the
  "Ready to Ship" copy, this must be confirmed (see Appendix).
- **Risk — fingerprint availability.** `wl list --json` does not return
  `currentFingerprint`, so `isAuditFresh` degrades to the 60 s time gate and a
  post-audit comment can falsely look stale, keeping "focus on audits" after
  audits complete. Mitigation: compute current fingerprints as the downtime
  worker/hydrator does, or add a purpose-built query.
- **Risk — misleading "Ready to Ship".** The 'S' ship shortcut is gated by the
  Ship Guard (live agent panes carrying this project's work-item IDs block
  shipping). "Ready to Ship" reflects audit state only; changing the guard is out
  of scope.
- **Assumption — condition structure preserved.** Only the deep-queue branch's
  copy changes; the banner still shows only when `isSprintComplete &&
  helpEnabled`.
- **Risk — missing test seams.** There is no existing banner test; the render
  pipeline is internal, so tests must use whatever seam the worklist suite
  already exercises, or expose a small pure helper for the copy decision.
- **Scope-creep risk:** do not touch the ship shortcut, Ship Guard, dispatch
  gating, or the queue-depth threshold. Capture extra opportunities as linked
  work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: What counts as an "outstanding audit"?**
  — Answer (research; no producer round): the freshness semantics already used
  across herdr — `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt, fingerprint,
  currentFingerprint)` returning false, or no stored `auditedAt`. Source:
  `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` (`isAuditFresh`), `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`
  (`inReviewBucket`), and the audit-dispatch tier in `downtime-worker.ts`.
  **ASSUMPTION — root-only scope chosen to match the existing banner count;

  `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (`openShipItDialog`, `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`) and

- *Interview style:* no producer interview round was required — the seed

# Diver docs stale: dive described as x-locked but implemented as diagonal (AH-0MUEI8HSU000QLEA)

## Problem statement

The Diver (E2) documentation still describes the dive as a **vertical drop with
x locked at the formation slot**, but the implemented and shipped behaviour
(AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX) is a **diagonal parabolic dive** toward the player
position snapshotted at dive start. The resulting docs contradict the code and
can mislead future implementation, tuning, and parity work.

## Users

- **Player / observer** — reads (or is described) the Diver as a predictable
  vertical threat; the real dive is diagonal toward the snapshotted player
  position, so the stated behaviour is wrong.
- **Developer / maintainer** — relies on `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  as the authoritative guide for enemy behaviour and gym/game parity; stale
  "x locked" wording risks re-introducing a vertical-only dive or mis-scoping
  related fixes.
- **Producer / reviewer** — needs the GDD and the implementation guide to agree
  on the dive contract so acceptance criteria for Diver work are unambiguous.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want the Diver documentation to describe the actual
  diagonal dive so that I do not implement or test against a vertical-only
  trajectory.
- As a **player-facing designer**, I want the GDD to state that a mid-dive aim
  change does not alter the in-flight arc, so the Diver's dodge window is
  understood correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Stale x-locked descriptions corrected:** The three known locations
  describe the dive as diagonal (both x and y follow the quadratic bezier from
  the formation slot to the player position snapshotted at dive start) and no
  longer state that x is locked:
  - `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1 catalog row (E2, "Vertical dive
    toward player (x locked at formation slot)").
  - `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §7.3 (live aim tracking, "Dives are
    x-locked at the formation slot.").
  - `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.1 (E2 Diver, "Dives straight down toward
    the player (x locked at its formation slot — a vertical trajectory)").
- [ ] **AC2 — Snapshot semantics documented:** The docs state that the dive
  target is snapshotted at dive start, so a mid-dive aim change does not alter
  the in-flight arc (§7.3 already carries this; it must remain consistent and be
  reflected in the corrected dive description).
- [ ] **AC3 — No stale vertical-only/x-locked Diver statements remain:** A
  repository search of `docs/` for the Diver dive finds no remaining
  x-locked / vertical-only trajectory claims for E2; the correction is
  cross-referenced to the superseding work item AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX.
- [ ] **AC4 — All related documentation is updated:** The three locations above
  are updated consistently (including the GDD and the implementation guide), and
  any relevant code comments remain accurate.
- [ ] **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Docs-only change** — no production code or runtime behaviour change; no test
  changes are expected. AC5 is a guard against accidental regressions.
- **Preserve existing documented semantics** — the formation-hold-while-away
  behaviour (`DIVING`/`PAUSING`/`RETURNING`, §7.6) and the "snapshot at dive
  start" seam decision are correct and must not be altered.
- **Keep GDD and implementation guide consistent** — both documents must describe
  the same dive contract; do not diverge or restate one as authoritative over the
  other without a reference.
- **Do not touch `CHANGELOG.md`** — it is managed by the ship skill's release
  pipeline.
- **No scope creep** — do not rewrite unrelated enemy documentation; record any
  additional discovered drift as a linked work item rather than folding it in.

## Existing state

- **Implemented behaviour (shipped, AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX):** `_startDive()` snapshots
  `this.target.x/y` into `_diveTargetX/Y`, computes `apexX=(startX+targetX)/2` and
  `apexY=GAME_HEIGHT*0.30`, and `_handleDive()` positions the Diver with
  `computeDivePoint(...)` — a quadratic bezier
  `P(t)=(1-t)²P0+2(1-t)tP1+t²P2` applied to **both** axes. The former x-lock
  (`setPosition(_diveStartX, point.y)`) has been removed. `setAimTarget()` documents
  the dive-start snapshot.
- **Stale docs (to be corrected):**
  - `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md:19` — catalog row: "Vertical dive
    toward player (x locked at formation slot)".
  - `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md:711` — §7.3: "Dives are x-locked at
    the formation slot." (the preceding sentence already correctly records the
    dive-start snapshot).
  - `docs/Game Design Document.md:196` — §4.1 E2 Diver: "Dives straight down
    toward the player (x locked at its formation slot — a vertical trajectory)".
    Note: the source work item labelled this §4.2; the current GDD places E2 in
    **§4.1 Enemy Types** (§4.2 is Wave/Formation Structures).
- A repository-wide search confirms these are the only Diver dive trajectory
  references in `docs/`; no test asserts the stale wording, so no test updates
  are required.

## Desired change

Correct the three documentation locations so they describe the diagonal
parabolic dive toward the player position snapshotted at dive start, retain and
make consistent the snapshot-at-dive-start wording, and cross-reference the
superseding work item AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX. No code, test, or behavioural change.

  diagonal toward the snapshotted player position and removed the x-lock; this

- **AH-0MUAYB957002EMYV — "Divers should not return"** (open) — adjacent Diver
  dive/return behaviour work that may touch the same docs sections (§7.6
  formation hold).
- **AH-0MTECNI8K008FSKH — "Implement: Core scene — enemy live aim tracking"**

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — recurring doc drift:** the GDD and the implementation guide duplicate
  the Diver dive contract, so a future behaviour change can re-stale one without

- No audio or visual beat indicators — silent internal scheduling only.

Refactor weapon fire rates as beat subdivisions and add catalogue-wide on-grid invariant

## Summary
Replace the hard-coded fire-rate constants in `src/utils/weapons.ts` with values derived from the 80 BPM beat period. Each weapon fires at an exact subdivision: cannon 2/beat (375 ms), spread 1/beat (750 ms), dual 1/beat (750 ms), rapid 6/beat (125 ms). Add a catalogue-wide test asserting every fire rate divides evenly into the beat period.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — All `WEAPON_*_FIRE_RATE` constants in `src/utils/weapons.ts` become derived from the beat period (e.g. `beatPeriodMs / subdivisions`), not hard-coded literals.
- [ ] **AC2** — `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` fire rates match the producer-specified values: cannon 375 ms (2/beat), spread 750 ms (1/beat), dual 750 ms (1/beat), rapid 125 ms (6/beat).
- [ ] **AC3** — A catalogue-wide invariant test asserts `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` for every weapon in `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`.
- [ ] **AC4** — Existing weapon tests still pass after the refactor (no behaviour change beyond timing).
- [ ] **AC5** — New weapons added to the catalogue must satisfy the invariant; the test fails if they do not.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC3** — [ ] **AC3 — Per-weapon subdivisions + catalogue-wide invariant.** Each weapon's fire interval is an exact subdivision of the beat: **cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat)**, **spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat)**. # Intake brief — Document gym-parity principle in AGENTS.md

**Headline:** The producer directive that gym scenes are the canonical parity reference for the game is currently implicit in the architecture notes but never stated as a rule; this item adds an explicit, discoverable gym-parity principle to the repo-local `AGENTS.md` so future agents and contributors apply gameplay changes consistently across the gyms and the game.

## Problem statement

Operators repeatedly see behaviour drift between the gym scenes and the shipped game. The producer's directive is that gyms and the game must execute the same core code, and that gym behaviours are the parity reference. That principle is **not stated as a rule** in the repo-local `AGENTS.md`, so it is easy for a contributor to change gameplay in one scene without updating the corresponding gym(s) — or vice versa — without violating any documented rule.

Verification performed: `grep -ni 'gym\|parity\|reference' AGENTS.md` returns no gym-parity rule (only generic workflow/documentation references). The `AGENTS.md` "Architecture Notes for Agents" section does describe the shared combat core and states that "no production scene keeps a divergent copy", but it does not state a general gym-parity rule or name the gym directories it applies to.

## Users

- **As an agent/contributor**, when I change a gameplay behaviour I want an explicit rule telling me to apply it consistently to the corresponding gym scene(s) and the game, so I do not silently introduce drift.
  - *"As a developer, when I change a player/enemy/projectile/power-up behaviour I want to know the gyms are the parity reference, so I update both in the same change."*
- **As a producer/reviewer**, when I audit a gameplay change I want a documented rule to point to, so I can verify parity was considered.
  - *"As the producer, I want gym parity stated in AGENTS.md so it is enforceable in review, not just implicit in architecture notes."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `AGENTS.md` contains an explicit gym-parity rule stating that gyms are the canonical parity reference for the game and that any gameplay-behaviour change must be applied consistently to the corresponding gym scene(s) and the game, unless a documented reason exists to diverge.
- **AC2** — The rule names the gym scenes/directories it applies to (at minimum `src/scenes/gym/`, including `src/scenes/gym/core/`, and the game-side scene/shared core such as `PlayScene` and `src/scenes/core/`), so a reader knows exactly which files are in scope.
- **AC3** — A docs review (grep/search across `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` and `docs/`) confirms there is no contradictory guidance that permits gyms to intentionally diverge without a documented reason; any near-conflicts are reconciled or explicitly noted.
- **AC4** — Validation: a reviewer can quote the AC1 rule from the rendered `AGENTS.md` and confirm it matches the producer directive; automated check is a grep asserting the rule text and the named directories are present.
- **AC5** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC6** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Additive only.** Do not weaken, reorder or remove any existing workflow/safety rule in `AGENTS.md`.
- **Consistent with existing architecture notes.** The rule must agree with the existing "Architecture Notes for Agents" shared-core description (no production scene keeps a divergent copy).
- **Docs-only change.** No application behaviour or source code behaviour changes.
- **UK English** spelling throughout.
- **Placement:** `AGENTS.md` currently has no "Game Architecture Conventions" or "Coding Disciplines" heading, so the rule is expected to be a new short section (e.g. `## Game Architecture Conventions`) placed near the existing `## Architecture Notes for Agents` section; final heading/placement is an implementation decision.

## Existing state

- `AGENTS.md` (repo-local) documents the agent workflow and Worklog usage, plus an `## Architecture Notes for Agents` section describing the shared two-tier combat core (`CombatCoreScene` → `CombatScene`) and the shared drop/bullet/enemy-fire layers. It states scenes must not keep divergent copies but has no explicit gym-parity rule.
- The gym scenes live in `src/scenes/gym/` (`GymBoss`, `GymCurveSequencer`, `GymEnemies`, `GymMinerals`, `GymPlayer`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymWeapons`) with the generic base `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`; the dev index is `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` and discovery is directory-dynamic via `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`.
- `README.md` documents the gym index as a dev-mode playground; `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` is the authoritative gym/enemy guide and already treats the shared core as the mechanism for parity.
- The wider parity effort is tracked by the epic **Gym↔game behavioural parity (AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA)** and the in-progress **Extend parity regression guard and cross-scene equivalence tests (AH-0MUII3GOO001XEBB)**.

## Desired change

Add a short, explicit rule to the repo-local `AGENTS.md` stating:

> Gyms are the canonical parity reference for the game. Any gameplay behaviour change must be applied consistently to the corresponding gym scene(s) and the game, unless a documented reason exists to diverge.

The rule should name the gym scenes/directories it applies to (`src/scenes/gym/`) and the game-side scene/shared core (`PlayScene`, `src/scenes/core/`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `AGENTS.md` — Add a new `## Game Architecture Conventions` section (or equivalent) containing the gym-parity rule; place near `## Architecture Notes for Agents`.
- `src/scenes/gym/` — The gym scene directory the rule names as in-scope (AC2); includes `core/GymFormationScene.ts`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — The shared core the parity rule points to.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Generic gym base consuming the shared core.
- `README.md` — References the gym index; verify the new rule does not contradict it (AC3).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Authoritative gym guide; verify consistency (AC3).

## Related work

- **Gym↔game behavioural parity: eliminate remaining core-code duplication so every object behaves identically (AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA)** — parent epic; this documentation rule supports its enforcement.
- **Extend parity regression guard and cross-scene equivalence tests (AH-0MUII3GOO001XEBB)** — in-progress automated parity guard this rule complements.
- **Speed power up should increase all speeds (AH-0MUAYB9JS0025YUB)** — `discovered-from`; the parity-drift incident that motivated this item.
- **Document scheme-aware gym controls (AH-0MTFRQR42009TYE9)** — precedent docs-only gym change.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — authoritative guide for gym/enemy implementation.
- `AGENTS.md` § *Architecture Notes for Agents* — existing shared-core guidance to remain consistent with.

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, add, always (+38 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The producer directive in the work item ("gyms are the canonical parity reference") is authoritative and should be quoted essentially verbatim.
- **Risk (scope creep):** Reconciling unrelated architecture-note content in `AGENTS.md` is out of scope; record extra opportunities as linked work items instead.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were required. The seed context supplied the exact rule text, the acceptance criteria and the verification performed; all remaining facts (gym directory, game-side scene, related parity work) were obtained from repo/worklog search, per the interview contract's "do not ask questions answerable by repo search" rule.
- **OPEN QUESTION:** none.

Effort/risk pre-check returned `decision: skip` (effort **Extra Small**, risk **Low**), so this docs-only item is small enough to implement directly and no child decomposition was created. The six automated review stages were run against the existing content:

# Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign

## Problem statement

**Wire the runtime auto-sequencer into the game's wave generation (AH-0MUH6LEYY0054E63)** makes the campaign all-or-nothing: with `sequencedWavesEnabled` off every level uses the hand-authored static `LEVELS`, and with it on *every* level is generated from the difficulty-curve config. A designer cannot hand-tune the levels that matter (onboarding, boss lead-in, a specific set-piece) while letting the sequencer ramp the rest. This item lets a single campaign **mix** generated and scripted levels, per level.

## Users

- As a **designer**, I want to mark individual levels as generated or scripted, so I can hand-tune onboarding and set-piece levels while the sequencer handles the rest.
- As a **player**, I want the campaign to keep its hand-authored early levels but ramp difficulty in later levels, so each run is both learnable and challenging.
- As a **maintainer**, I want a single, data-driven campaign definition whose generated and scripted sources are explicit and testable, so the two paths cannot silently diverge.

## Existing state

- **Campaign builder** — `buildSequencedLevels(rows?, candidates?)` in `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` groups `DifficultyCurveRow[]` by level, calls the read-only `sequencer()` once per generated level with `defaultShootEnabled = level >= FIRST_FIRING_LEVEL (4)`, converts `ShootableWave.groups` to `WaveGroup`s and returns `LevelDefinition[]`. On empty/degenerate input or a sequencer throw it returns static `LEVELS` (whole-campaign fallback). It has **no notion of a per-level source**.
- **Config** — `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` is one row per `(level, wave)` with columns `level,levelName,wave,targetDifficulty`; loaded by `loadDifficultyCurves()` (`src/core/configStore.ts`) through the CSV pipeline (dev `/api/csv/...`, bundled `?raw` in production) with `defaultDifficultyCurves()` computed from the static `LEVELS` calibration as the fallback. Types live in `src/core/configTypes.ts` (`DifficultyCurveRow`); codec/validator in `src/core/csv.ts` (`parseDifficultyCurves` / `serializeDifficultyCurves` / `validateDifficultyCurveRow`).
- **Static campaign** — `LEVELS` in `src/waves/Formations.ts`: five `LevelDefinition`s (names, waves, `shootEnabled`). Levels 1–3 do not fire; 4–5 do (GDD §2.4/§2.5).
- **Wiring** — `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` is being wired (in-progress child **Opt-in toggle and PlayScene wiring (AH-0MUITS1SM008GPR9)**) to read the opt-in `sequencedWavesEnabled` toggle and, when on, call `buildSequencedLevels()` and inject the result via `WaveManager.setLevels()`. `WaveManager` already accepts injected `LevelDefinition[]` and defaults to `LEVELS`.

## Desired change

Extend the campaign builder so each level's source is selectable, and merge the two sources into one `LevelDefinition[]`:

- A level marked **`generated`** is produced by `sequencer()` from that level's curve rows (as today, with `shootEnabled` from the level's fire rule).
- A level marked **`scripted`** is taken **byte-for-byte from static `LEVELS`** (its own waves and its own `shootEnabled`), and is not passed to the sequencer.
- The campaign skeleton, the config representation of the selector, and the fallback scope are the three decisions in **Open questions** below; the proposed answers are the recommended options there.

When `sequencedWavesEnabled` is **off**, behaviour is unchanged: static `LEVELS` exactly. Mixed mode is only reachable with the toggle on.

## Acceptance criteria (draft — pending Open questions)

- **Per-level source selection** — a campaign can be configured with a mix of generated and scripted levels; `buildSequencedLevels()` returns the correct source per level (test asserts a mixed config yields scripted levels identical to the matching `LEVELS` entries and generated levels differing from static `LEVELS`).
- **Scripted levels are exact** — every scripted level's `LevelDefinition` (name, wave count, groups, spacing, positions and `shootEnabled`) is deeply equal to the corresponding static `LEVELS` definition (byte-for-byte in intent; test asserts deep equality).
- **Generated levels unchanged** — a generated level in a mixed campaign is identical to the same level built by today's all-generated builder for the same curve and candidate pool (determinism preserved; no RNG/clock/I-O).
- **Fire rule respected per source** — generated levels 1–3 have `shootEnabled=false` and 4+ `true`; scripted levels keep `LEVELS`' own flags (test asserts both).
- **Fallback is safe** — a missing/empty/malformed curve for a generated level, or an empty candidate pool, never produces an unplayable campaign: the affected level (or campaign, per the Open question decision) falls back to static `LEVELS` and the game does not crash (test covers each case).
- **Runtime wiring** — with the toggle on and a mixed config, `PlayScene` runs the mixed campaign via `WaveManager`; with the toggle off it runs static `LEVELS` exactly (test asserts both paths at the scene seam).
- **Testing/validation** — new/updated unit and integration tests cover the selector parsing, mixed merge, scripted deep-equality, generated equivalence, fire rule and fallback, and they are meaningful and passing.
- **Documentation** — all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the README, `docs/Game Design Document.md` and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
- **No regressions** — the full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`).

## Constraints

- **Pure core stays pure** — `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` must not be modified (read-only call site).
- **Determinism** — generation remains a pure function of config + candidate pool; scripted levels are static data.
- **No behavioural change when the toggle is off** — existing `WaveManager`/`PlayScene`/campaign tests pass unchanged.
- **CSV pipeline is the source of truth** — any new config goes through the existing codec/`configStore`/Vite plugin pattern; malformed rows must not crash.
- **Backwards compatibility** — the existing 4-column `difficulty-curves.csv` and `defaultDifficultyCurves()` must keep working; existing tests pass unchanged.
- UK English in prose; Markdown in the work item.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — add per-level source selection and the scripted/generated merge; keep the fallback guard.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` — mixed-campaign tests (source selection, scripted deep-equality, generated equivalence, fallback).
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — extend `DifficultyCurveRow` with the source field (if the explicit-selector option is chosen).
- `src/core/csv.ts` — extend the difficulty-curve codec/validator for the source field.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — add the per-level source column/rows (if the explicit-selector option is chosen).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — keep `loadDifficultyCurves()` / `defaultDifficultyCurves()` consistent with the selector.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — static `LEVELS` referenced as the scripted source (read-only).
- `src/core/rules.ts` — `sequencedWavesEnabled` toggle (existing; only a settings-store selector option would change it).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — already injects the built campaign; verify mixed campaigns flow through unchanged.
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — whitelist/validation if the CSV schema changes.
- Test files: `src/core/csv.test.ts`, `src/core/configStore.test.ts`, `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`.
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§2.4/§2.5), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§9 sequencer), `README.md`.

## Related work

- **Wire the runtime auto-sequencer into the game's wave generation (AH-0MUH6LEYY0054E63)** — the opt-in wiring this builds on; defers mixed campaigns to this item.
- **Implement runtime auto-sequencer for dynamic difficulty adjustment (AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X)** — delivered `sequencer()`.
- **Campaign builder: config to generated level definitions (AH-0MUITS0VD000DVSV)** — delivered `buildSequencedLevels()` (completed).
- **Difficulty-curve config, codec and CSV loader (AH-0MUITRZZE000OYQE)** — delivered the CSV schema/codec this item may extend (completed).
- **Opt-in toggle and PlayScene wiring (AH-0MUITS1SM008GPR9)** — the wiring this depends on (in-progress).
- **Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL)** — designer tool for curves; out of scope here.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §2.4/§2.5 fire rules, §3.2 level themes.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §9 enemy difficulty scoring / sequencer.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Config-schema churn** — an explicit `source` column changes `DifficultyCurveRow`, the codec and the CSV that a just-completed child defined; mitigated by making the field default to `generated` so existing rows/tests are unaffected (if that option is chosen).
- **Fallback scope** — a whole-campaign fallback on one bad generated level would silently discard a designer's other scripted/generated choices; the recommended per-level fallback avoids this (see Open questions).
- **Scripted numbering** — a level marked scripted whose number has no `LEVELS` entry is undefined; must be handled explicitly (fallback or reject) rather than crashing.
- **Scope creep** — runtime curve editing (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL) and any sequencer-algorithm change are out of scope; extra opportunities are recorded as linked work items.
- **Assumption (toggle interaction)** — mixed mode is only active when `sequencedWavesEnabled` is on; when off, static `LEVELS` is used unchanged.
- **Assumption (scripted source is `LEVELS`)** — scripted levels are referenced by level number into static `LEVELS`; no new hand-authored wave data is introduced.

## Open questions (producer review required)

1. **How should the per-level source selector be declared?** Options: (a) explicit `source` column in `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` (`generated`|`scripted`); (b) presence/absence of curve rows (a level with no rows is scripted); (c) a separate settings-store or CSV selector (e.g. `GameRules.scriptedLevels: number[]`). **Recommended: (a)** — explicit and colocated with the curve, matching "mark individual levels"; requires `targetDifficulty` to be optional for scripted rows. This is a schema change to `DifficultyCurveRow`/codec/CSV.
2. **What determines the campaign skeleton and ordering when mixing?** Options: (a) start from all static `LEVELS`, override the configured levels per their source, and append generated levels numbered beyond `LEVEL_COUNT`; (b) the campaign is exactly the configured levels, with scripted ones referencing `LEVELS` by number; (c) all static levels are scripted by default and only configured levels are generated. **Recommended: (a)** — preserves the shipped five-level campaign and guarantees onboarding levels exist.
3. **What is the fallback scope when a generated level has no usable curve?** Options: (a) per-level — use that level's static `LEVELS` definition if one exists, otherwise skip/apply a safe guard; (b) whole-campaign — fall back to all of static `LEVELS` (current builder behaviour); (c) per-level for a bad level, whole-campaign only when the entire config is empty. **Recommended: (a)** — one bad level must not discard the rest of a mixed campaign.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (Round 1): How should the per-level source selector be declared?** — **OPEN QUESTION**; awaiting producer. Recommended: explicit `source` column in `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`. Source: asynchronous producer-review handoff (auto-dispatched downtime run; no interactive approver).
- **Q (Round 1): What determines the campaign skeleton and ordering when mixing?** — **OPEN QUESTION**; awaiting producer. Recommended: start from all static `LEVELS`, override per source, append generated levels beyond `LEVEL_COUNT`. Source: asynchronous producer-review handoff.
- **Q (Round 1): What is the fallback scope when a generated level has no usable curve?** — **OPEN QUESTION**; awaiting producer. Recommended: per-level fallback to the matching static `LEVELS` definition. Source: asynchronous producer-review handoff.
- **Assumption (documented, not asked): mixed mode is only active while `sequencedWavesEnabled` is on.** Evidence: `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` is reached only from the toggle path in `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (AH-0MUITS1SM008GPR9).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU7JTF9W008B8HW** – Player cannot move during wave/level transition pauses (completed)
- **AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZY** – Need juice when the player is destroyed (completed)
- **AH-0MUD9R4BA004WQEM** – Cross-scene equivalence tests and duplicate-body verification (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, algorithm, auto, boss, builder (+62 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mudiwetp003xc3x, auto, boss, builder, builds (+55 more)

# Intake brief — Harvester enemy

**Headline:** Add a Harvester enemy archetype — a large, slow, roaming enemy
that actively seeks and absorbs the nearest mineral and survives five player
bullets — plus the shared multi-hit health support and mineral-seeker seam it
needs in both the shipped game and the enemy gym.

## Problem statement

The bestiary currently has no enemy that competes with the player for
minerals. Non-asteroid enemies already absorb any mineral they happen to
overlap (GDD §4.4.1), but none deliberately hunts the field. The Harvester
introduces a mineral-denial threat: it actively drives to the nearest mineral,
is large (easy to hit and quick to absorb), slow to cross the screen, and
durable (five hits), forcing the player to spend ammunition and attention on it
before it strips the field.

## Users

- **As a player**, I want a durable enemy that actively steals minerals, so
  that collecting minerals becomes a contest rather than a free pickup.
- **As a player**, I want the Harvester to be large and slow, so that the
  five-hit cost is fair and readable rather than punishing.
- **As a designer**, I want to tune the Harvester (size, colour, speed,
  health, score) through the existing CSV/enemy-config pipeline without
  touching scene code.
- **As a developer**, I want multi-hit health and mineral seeking to be shared,
  data-driven capabilities, so future multi-hit or seeking enemies are cheap
  and the game and gyms cannot diverge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — New `harvester` archetype is registered and discoverable.** A
  `harvester` row exists in `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` with a matching seed
  fallback in `src/core/configDefaults.ts`, is mapped in
  `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`, appears in the gym index, and spawns/renders
  in `GymEnemies`. Verified by config/CSV tests and a gym spawn test.
- [ ] **AC2 — Mineral-seeking behaviour.** The Harvester moves toward the
  nearest live mineral at its configured (slow) speed and absorbs it on
  overlap using the existing enemy-absorption rule, incrementing its tracked
  mineral count. When no mineral exists it holds station / continues its idle
  drift (per Q2). Verified by deterministic entity + scene tests that place
  minerals and assert the Harvester closes distance and consumes them.
- [ ] **AC3 — Five-hit destruction.** The Harvester survives exactly five
  player-bullet hits. Each non-lethal hit consumes the bullet and produces
  readable feedback; the fifth hit destroys it, plays destruction audio/VFX
  exactly once, awards its score, advances wave accounting, and re-drops
  25–50 % of absorbed minerals per the existing rule. Verified by a
  five-hit test and a single-destruction/single-audio regression test.
- [ ] **AC4 — Existing enemies are unchanged.** All current 1-HP enemies
  (Scout, Diver, Tank, Phaser, Swarm, Asteroid) remain destroyed by one hit and
  their tests stay green.
- [ ] **AC5 — Game ↔ gym parity.** The Harvester's seek, absorption and
  five-hit destruction run through the same shared code path in `PlayScene` and
  in `GymEnemies` (per the gym-parity principle); no scene re-implements the
  behaviour.
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing/validation.** New unit/integration tests cover: config
  codec round-trip (including any new health column), factory mapping, seek
  target selection (nearest mineral; none present), absorption counting,
  five-hit destruction, and a `PlayScene` + `GymEnemies` parity check. Full
  project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
  the changes, including the Game Design Document enemy catalog / health model
  (§2.3, §4.1, §4.4.1, §6.5), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  (§1/§8 enemy catalog and add-an-enemy checklist), the README enemy list, and
  code comments.

## Constraints

- **Data-driven:** tuning lives in the CSV/enemy-config pipeline; no new
  per-enemy scene or hard-coded archetype branch.
- **Single source of truth:** no duplication of collision, mineral-collection,
  or health logic — this is a hard requirement of the gym-parity epic
  (`AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`).
- **No regression:** existing 1-HP enemies and their tests must be untouched
  semantically.
- **Surgical:** match existing entity/config/scene style; do not delete
  unrelated dead code (report it instead).
- **UK English** in all written output and documentation.
- **Gating:** implementation proceeds only through `/skill:implement`; this
  intake does not authorise code changes.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-27 against HEAD)

- Enemy archetypes are **data, not code**: `EnemyConfig` (`src/core/configTypes.ts`),
  one CSV row per archetype (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`), seed fallbacks in
  `src/core/configDefaults.ts`, factory mapping in `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`.
- All regular enemies are **1 HP** (destroyed by a single bullet) and the GDD
  states this explicitly (`docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.3, §4.1, §6.5).
  Only the Boss is multi-hit (4-phase). There is an optional `takeDamage?()`
  seam on entities (`CombatCoreScene`, `CombatScene`, `GymFormationScene`), but
  the shared generic path currently calls it **without** running
  `onEnemyDestroyed()`/destruction audio when the entity finally dies — that
  is a gap this work must close for a multi-hit regular enemy to score, drop
  minerals and advance waves correctly.
- The Asteroid is the precedent for a **non-formation roamer**: it has
  `formationKind: single`, overrides `updatePosition(dt)` (called by the gym
  and game before `applyFormationPosition`) and `applyFormationPosition` is a
  no-op.
- Minerals already exist: `Mineral` (`src/entities/Mineral.ts`), collection and
  non-asteroid absorption in `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`
  (`collectMinerals`), kill re-drop in `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts`,
  and the 25–50 % re-drop fraction in `src/core/rules.ts`. `BaseEnemy` already
  tracks `mineralCount` / `collectMineral()` / `mineralRedropCount()`.
- The shared enemy-fire dispatcher (`src/entities/enemyFire.ts`) already
  mentions the "planned Harvester" as the example of a one-line wiring change.

## Desired change

1. Generalise enemy health data-driven (pending Q1) so a regular enemy can
   require N hits, and make the shared collision path correctly finalise a
   multi-hit kill (audio, `onEnemyDestroyed`, drops, wave accounting).
2. Add a `Harvester` entity that roams (like the Asteroid) and steers toward
   the nearest live mineral, absorbing it on overlap.
3. Register the archetype (CSV + seed + factory + score) and expose it in the
   gym.
4. Integrate it into the campaign per Q3 (roadmap: available in the gym and as
   a rare roaming spawn in later levels).
5. Update the GDD/ENEMY design docs/README for the health-model and enemy
   catalog changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — New `harvester` row; add a `health` column if
  Q1 is answered "data-driven".
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — `health` field on `EnemyConfig` (if data-driven).
- `src/core/csv.ts` — `health` column in `ENEMY_COLUMN_ORDER`, coercion and
  validation.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — `harvester` seed fallback (+ default health).
- `src/entities/Harvester.ts` — New roamer entity: slow seek movement, large
  body, multi-hit health, no firing.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — Shared multi-hit health / `takeDamage`
  behaviour (or a small shared health helper).
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — Map `harvester` → `Harvester`.
- `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` — No-firing archetype handling (existing fallback
  to aimed fire must be avoided for the Harvester).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — Finalise a multi-hit kill through
  `onEnemyDestroyed` + destruction audio; supply the live mineral field to
  seeking entities.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Wire seeking/minerals, score value, roamer
  movement, wave/score accounting.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` + `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` —
  Expose the same mineral list/seek seam and multi-hit path.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` / `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts` /
  `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — Campaign spawn integration per Q3.
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — Optional `health` difficulty factor
  (recommended follow-up, not necessarily in scope).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`,
  `README.md` — Documentation updates.
- Tests: `src/entities/Harvester.test.ts`,
  `src/entities/enemyFactory.test.ts`, `src/core/csv.test.ts`,
  `src/core/enemyConfig.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.

## Related work

- `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` — Gym↔game behavioural-parity epic (critical, open).
  This work must consume the shared cores it establishes and must not add a new
  divergence.
- `AH-0MUII3BBW000XZ46` — Shared enemy-fire dispatch (completed). Names the
  Harvester as the exemplar of one-line fire wiring.
- `AH-0MUII3DHM008L7JF` — Shared mineral layer: collection, hold/overflow,
  choice overlay (completed).
- `AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB` — Gym asteroids do not drop minerals / shared
  kill-drop rule (open); relevant to the re-drop path.
- `AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F` — E6 Asteroid non-formation roamer (completed).
  Precedent architecture for a roaming enemy.
- `AH-0MT7V5UH90023XWR` — Clarify enemy health / one-hit destruction model in
  GDD (completed). The GDD currently pins regular enemies at 1 HP; a 5-HP
  regular enemy requires an explicit, documented revision (see Q1).
- `AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K` — Enemy difficulty scoring (completed). Health is not
  currently a scored factor (see Risks).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — health-model conflict.** A 5-HP regular enemy contradicts the GDD's
  explicit "all regular enemies (E1–E5) are 1 HP" and "no multi-hit bullet"
  rules. Mitigation: settle Q1 before implementation and update the GDD.
- **Risk — multi-hit kill does not finalise.** The current
  `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy` `takeDamage` branch skips `onEnemyDestroyed` and
  destruction audio. Mitigation: extend the shared seam and pin it with a test
  so score/wave/drop/audio happen exactly once on the killing blow.
- **Risk — seek seam duplication.** Giving the entity the mineral list must be
  done once in the shared collision/tick path, not copied into each scene
  (parity epic). Mitigation: add a single `setSeekTargets`/equivalent seam
  alongside the existing `setAimTarget`.
- **Risk — difficulty under-scoring.** `enemyDifficulty` has no health factor,
  so a 5-HP enemy may score lower than its true threat. Mitigation: record a
  linked follow-up work item; do not let it block this feature.
- **Risk — scope creep into wave/level design.** Wiring a new roamer into the
  campaign can balloon. Mitigation: Q3 fixes scope up front; keep the gym
  demonstration as the minimum and a rare campaign spawn as the target.
- **Assumption — "collects it" reuses existing absorption.** The Harvester
  absorbs the mineral on overlap and tallies it; on death it re-drops 25–50 %
  per the existing rule. (Confirm via Q2.)
- **Assumption — tuning values are implementation/gym choices.** "Large" and
  "slow" are the requirements; exact px size/speed/colour are chosen and tuned
  in the gym (indicative: size ≈ 40–48 px, speed ≈ 20–30 px/s).
- **Assumption — the Harvester does not fire** unless Q2 says otherwise.

## Open questions (routed to the producer)

These are recorded as a comment and repeated here; the item is flagged
`needs-producer-review`.

1. **Health model (blocking).** A 5-HP regular enemy breaks the GDD's explicit
   1-HP model. Options: (a) generalise health data-driven (new `health` CSV
   column + GDD update; P4 Bomb still deals no damage); (b) keep a
   Harvester-only code constant; (c) something else. **Recommended:** (a) — it
   is the smallest durable change, serves future multi-hit enemies, and keeps
   tuning in the CSV. Sub-question: should each non-lethal hit show a health
   indicator (e.g. colour/scale change), or is ordinary hit feedback enough?
2. **Mineral-seeking semantics (blocking).** Options: (a) always seek the
   nearest live mineral anywhere on the field; absorb on overlap; no firing;
   cannot steal from the player's hold; re-drop per the existing 25–50 % rule.
   (b) only seek minerals within a detection radius. (c) also fire at the
   player. **Recommended:** (a) — it matches "moves towards the nearest
   mineral" literally and reuses the whole existing mineral layer.
3. **Spawn / campaign integration (blocking).** Options: (a) available in the
   gym **and** added to the campaign as a rare roaming spawn in later levels;
   (b) gym-only archetype for now; (c) a fixed formation group. **Recommended:**
   (a) — it makes the enemy playable in the campaign and visible in the gym,
   which is where tuning happens.
4. *(Non-blocking)* Score value and difficulty weight. **Recommended:** score
   ≈ 400 (durable, between Tank 300 and Boss phases) and a linked follow-up to
   add a `health` factor to `enemyDifficulty`, rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix — clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (health model) — **OPEN QUESTION**; awaiting producer answer. Options and
  recommendation recorded above (recommended: data-driven `health` column +
  GDD update; P4 Bomb unchanged).
- Q2 (mineral-seeking semantics) — **OPEN QUESTION**; awaiting producer answer
  (recommended: seek nearest live mineral anywhere; no firing; existing absorb
  and re-drop; no hold theft).
- Q3 (spawn / campaign integration) — **OPEN QUESTION**; awaiting producer

# Test: shared mineral kill-drop rule

Test-first task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC3, AC5).

## Goal

Write deterministic unit + guard tests that pin the contract of the shared mineral kill-drop rule **before** it is implemented, so `PlayScene` and the gyms provably share one rule.

## Required coverage

- Small asteroid (`getSizeTier() === 'small'`) → exactly one mineral drop at the asteroid's death position.

- Non-asteroid enemy that absorbed N minerals → re-drops between `mineralRedropFractionMin` and `mineralRedropFractionMax` of N, never more than N, at the death site, using a seeded RNG for determinism.
- Non-asteroid enemy with 0 absorbed minerals → no drops.
- Re-drop scatter stays within `MINERAL_REDROP_SCATTER_RADIUS` of the death site.

Make every formation gym (including `GymMinerals` and the `GymEnemies` asteroid row) drop minerals on enemy destruction exactly as the game does, by calling the shared helper.

- Call it from both the generic destruction path (`onEnemyDestroyed`) and the EXPLODE button (`explodeRandom`), so every destruction path drops exactly once.
- Keep the existing asteroid-split config seam unchanged (splitting stays scene/config-specific).
- Update the `GymMinerals` / `GymFormationScene` docstrings to describe the shared code path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Gyms drop on small-asteroid destruction.** Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` / `GymEnemies` asteroid row spawns exactly one mineral at its position.

- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid drop + non-asteroid re-drop) has one production definition that both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` consume.
- Large and medium asteroids drop none directly; their small split children do.
- The gym test suites added by the test-first task pass, and `npm test` plus `npm run typecheck` pass.
